author: potuz
content: Oh I thought we moved it back to 600ms, at least that landed in develop I think. I'll check but yeah we made that configurable and default to something much shorter after measuring in devnet. For direct connection builders 600 ms is more than fine for most operators and if you live in the middle of Africa with a bad connection you can modify it. Also arguably the best strategy for an operator that wants to play timing games is not to  give a longer delay but rather request multiple times with a shorter one, so we'll make that configurable as well just in case

author: daniellehrner
content: I am working on improving our response time as well, but I was just wondering why it is that much shorter than other CLs. But thanks for the explanation I think I understand now

author: potuz
content: Yeah I think other CLs are giving the relay the right to decide on the block viability by setting it that long by default

author: nflaig
content: why do you use the same timeout for `engine_getPayloadV6`, I don't see a technical reason for this, even if all builder bids time out for some reason, better to wait for engine to respond and give more time rather than missing the payload entirely

author: nflaig
content: the cutoff only needs to be there so the beacon block itself isn't too late, if neither builder nor EL responds in time, do other clients already put a dummy bid into the beacon block as a worst case fallback?

author: potuz
content: For getPayload is tricky and probably it's about simplicity. I guess we could keep waiting if there's no bid as a last resort or put a self built envelope that we just don't broadcast. I'll try to add this option. But in principle I don't want to have a timeout that delays block broadcast when we already have received bids and could send the block as early as we want

author: nflaig
content: case I am thinking about if if circuit breaker is active and EL is slow to respond, in that case need to cut it at some point and put in a dummy bid
